A889DA.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the timings over the runs that stayed on the issued route, and the clause beside it records that about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route. The claim is about delivery time on the runs the routing change was rolled out to, so the population is every run dispatched and the minute figures describe roughly five sixths of it. A run leaves the issued route when it meets a blockage or a diversion, which is exactly what makes a run come in long, so an average taken over the runs that stayed on it sits below the figure for all runs dispatched, and the reductions of 8, 5, 9 and 6 minutes are consistent with no reduction at all. Every case is vans out of Kettleby Wharf in February under dispatcher Verhoeven, so one and the same exclusion sits under all four groups at once. The four cases differ only in log serial, clock time, terminal and desk - surface detail that rules nothing out, so the evidence is exactly as dependent as the coherent version.

The timings exclude the runs most likely to be slow: 'Timings cover the runs that stayed on the issued route, and about a sixth of each depot's runs left the issued route.' That compliant subset is compared to all runs a month earlier, so the 5-9 minute saving is a selection artefact as much as a routing effect.

Same exclusion named, with the correct point that the dropped runs are the slow ones.

4969DF.confound_note: All four cohorts are 40 Fenwick users on Corvid 7 phones inside one March, and the single weather fact stated mid-passage covers every case at once: outdoor temperature in each cohort's city ran about four degrees below the month before, a shift that lowers resting heart rate on its own. The scope clause beside that fact has every cohort sleeping in rooms with no climate control, which carries the cooling to every user whose heart rate was read. Each cohort is compared against itself in February, under warmer nights, rather than against an unenrolled cohort in the same month. The cooling and the app arrived together, leaving the 3 to 6 bpm drops unattributable to the app. The population and completeness clauses in the same line leave the readings covering every enrolled user; nothing further is wrong with the item.
descriptions: A named alternative cause reaches every cohort: 'Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city ran about four degrees below the month before, and every cohort slept in rooms with no climate control', so the colder sleeping environment applied to all four cohorts over exactly the comparison window and could itself account for the 3-6 bpm drop.

'Outdoor temperature in each cohort's city ran about four degrees below the month before, and every cohort slept in rooms with no climate control' - with no climate control the outdoor drop reaches the sleeping rooms, so a colder sleeping environment is a named alternative cause of the 3-6 bpm fall that applies to all four cohorts.
match_notes: Names the stated temperature drop plus the no-climate-control clause that carries it to every cohort.
Same confound, correctly traced through the uncontrolled sleeping rooms to all four cohorts.
